toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Analyzer B is very likely fine. One Level 2 potassium QC result failed. The re-pour passed 21 minutes later. Levels 1 and 3 were normal. Level 2 means are unchanged since the lot change. QC was run on schedule (182 of 182 runs). A single flag like this is expected by chance about once or twice a month. Patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agree within 0.02 mmol/L on average, and the patient median on B is stable. So the data don't support a lot problem, a systematic fault, or skipped QC. I can't say whether the cause was a sampling glitch or chance, and I wouldn't record either as confirmed.

Ward 6's high potassiums split evenly between the two analyzers. Most of them had samples delayed over 3 hours since the tube station failed. Four renal overflow patients also arrived. That points to transport delay and patient mix, not analyzer error. This link is likely but not proven. No repeat samples have been requested.

What to sign off: return B to service and close the 186-result review with no amendments. Keep the lot in use. Don't widen the limits and don't recall results. Consider an extra Level 2 QC at the start of each shift for a week. Ask Ward 6 for fresh samples from the high-result patients, and push for the tube repair.
